examples.en: Two boys suddenly got into a fistfight in the hallway.
Brothers shouldn't fistfight. Settle it with words.
The players almost got into a fistfight during the game.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 동생이랑 자주 주먹다짐하면서 컸어요.
examples.en: When we were little, I grew up often scuffling with my younger sibling.
They got into a fistfight and both got scolded by the teacher.
I saw people fistfighting on the bus.

explain: '싸우다'는 말싸움이든 몸싸움이든 다 쓰지만, 이 말은 주먹을 주고받는 몸싸움에 써요. 말로 하는 싸움은 '말다툼'이라고 해요. '주먹다짐을 하다'처럼 명사로도 자주 써요.
explain_en: '싸우다' covers both verbal and physical fights, but this word is for fights where fists are exchanged. A verbal fight is '말다툼'. You will also often see it as a noun: '주먹다짐을 하다'.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 웃을 때 주먹코가 더 귀여워요.
examples.en: My younger sibling's round nose looks even cuter when they smile.
I have a bulbous nose, so my glasses keep sliding down.
I take after my dad, so I have a bulbous nose too.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 주먹코인데도 인기가 아주 많아요.
examples.en: That actor is very popular even though he has a bulbous nose.

examples.ko: 주먹코를 작아 보이게 하는 화장법이 있어요?
examples.en: Is there a makeup technique that makes a bulbous nose look smaller?

examples.ko: 코끝이 둥글고 큰 주먹코는 인상이 푸근해 보여요.
examples.en: A round, big-tipped nose gives a warm, comfortable impression.

explain: 코끝이 둥글고 뭉툭한 코를 말해요. 콧구멍이 위쪽으로 보이는 코는 '들창코', 콧등이 휘어 있는 코는 '매부리코'라고 해서 모양마다 이름이 달라요. 남의 얼굴을 말할 때는 놀리는 느낌이 될 수 있으니 조심하세요.
explain_en: It describes a nose with a round, blunt tip. Other shapes have other names, such as '들창코' (upturned nostrils) and '매부리코' (hooked nose). Be careful when using it about someone else's face, since it can sound like teasing.

examples.en: Mom kneaded my shoulders for me.
The child plays, squeezing and kneading the clay.
If you knead the dough with your hands, it gets soft.
Add the seasoning to the meat and work it in with your hands.
I've developed a habit of squeezing a stress ball over and over.
Please don't squish the puppy's cheeks too much.

explain: 손으로 쥐었다 폈다 하면서 계속 만지는 모습이에요. 안마, 반죽, 찰흙처럼 손으로 주무르는 일에 써요. 기본 말인 '주무르다'보다 같은 동작을 되풀이하는 모습이 더 잘 보여요. '조물조물'은 작고 가볍게 만질 때 더 어울려요.
explain_en: It shows squeezing and releasing something with your hands again and again, as in massage, dough or clay. Compared with the basic verb '주무르다', it brings out the repeated motion more. '조물조물' fits smaller, lighter touches better.

examples.ko: 저는 주변머리가 없어서 처음 보는 사람과 말을 못 해요.
examples.en: I have no social knack, so I can't talk to people I've just met.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 주변머리가 있어서 어디서나 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: That friend is resourceful and gets along well anywhere.

examples.ko: 그렇게 주변머리도 없어서 어떻게 장사를 해요?
examples.en: With so little knack for getting by, how will you run a shop?

examples.ko: 주변머리만 조금 있었어도 취직이 쉬웠을 거예요.
examples.en: If I'd had just a little knack for getting by, finding a job would have been easy.

examples.ko: 주변머리 없는 제 성격이 가끔 답답해요.
examples.en: I sometimes find my clumsy, unresourceful personality frustrating.

examples.ko: 그는 주변머리는 없지만 마음은 정말 따뜻해요.
examples.en: He lacks social savvy, but he is really warm-hearted.

explain: 일을 잘 해결하거나 사람들과 요령 있게 지내는 재주를 말해요. 대부분 '주변머리가 없다'처럼 부정으로 쓰고, 답답한 사람을 약간 흉볼 때 나와요. 비슷한 말로 '융통성'이나 '눈치'가 있지만, 이 말이 더 구어적이고 거칠어요.
explain_en: It refers to the knack for handling things and getting along with people smoothly. It is mostly used negatively, as in '주변머리가 없다', when mildly criticizing someone who seems stiff or clumsy. Words like '융통성' and '눈치' are close, but this one is more colloquial and blunt.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁 모임의 주빈은 김 교수님이에요.
examples.en: The guest of honor at tonight's gathering is Professor Kim.
When the guest of honor arrived, everyone stood up.
We invited my uncle as the guest of honor for this event.

examples.ko: 주빈께 먼저 음식을 드리는 게 예의예요.
examples.en: It is good manners to serve the guest of honor first.

examples.ko: 주빈을 위해 가장 좋은 자리를 비워 뒀어요.
examples.en: We kept the best seat empty for the guest of honor.

examples.ko: 주빈 옆자리에 앉게 되어서 많이 긴장했어요.
examples.en: I was very nervous to be seated next to the guest of honor.

explain: 잔치나 행사에서 가장 귀하게 모시는 손님이에요. 같은 자리에 온 손님 가운데 중심이 되는 사람이라서, 손님을 맞는 쪽은 '주인'이라고 해요. '귀빈'은 높고 귀한 손님 전체를 말하고, '주인공'은 행사의 중심이 되는 사람이에요.
explain_en: It is the most honored guest at a banquet or event. The side that welcomes guests is the '주인' (host). '귀빈' means any distinguished guest, while '주인공' means the central person of the occasion.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 주산 학원에 다녀서 암산이 빨라요.
examples.en: I went to an abacus academy as a kid, so my mental math is fast.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 주산으로 계산을 아주 빨리 하세요.
examples.en: My grandfather calculates very fast with an abacus.

examples.ko: 요즘은 계산기가 있어서 주산을 배우는 사람이 적어요.
examples.en: These days there are calculators, so few people learn abacus calculation.
Abacus calculation was famous as a kind of brain training.

examples.ko: 주산과 암산을 같이 가르치는 교실이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a class that teaches abacus and mental math together.
I practice every day to enter an abacus competition.

explain: 계산 도구는 '주판'이고, 그 주판으로 하는 계산 방법이 '주산'이에요. 주판 없이 머릿속으로 하는 계산은 '암산'이라고 해요. 옛날 학원 이야기나 어른들 대화에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The tool is the '주판' (abacus), and the calculation method done with it is '주산'. Calculating in your head without one is '암산'. It often comes up when older people talk about old-style academies.

examples.en: Jeju Island is the main producing region for tangerines.
This area is famous as a major apple-growing region.

examples.ko: 주산지에서 직접 사면 더 싸고 신선해요.
examples.en: If you buy directly in the main producing area, it's cheaper and fresher.

examples.ko: 올해 비가 많이 와서 주산지의 작황이 나빠요.
examples.en: It rained a lot this year, so the harvest in the main growing area is poor.
Do you know where the main garlic-producing region is?

examples.ko: 배추 주산지를 찾아가서 김장 재료를 샀어요.
examples.en: I went to a main cabbage-growing area and bought the kimchi-making ingredients.

explain: 어떤 농산물이나 물건이 가장 많이 나는 지역이에요. 보통 '사과 주산지'처럼 앞에 물건 이름을 붙여요. '원산지'는 처음 나온 곳이나 표시에 쓰는 원래 출처이고, '생산지'는 만들어진 곳이라 서로 달라요.
explain_en: It is the region where a crop or product is produced the most, usually with the item in front, as in '사과 주산지'. It differs from '원산지' (origin, as on labels) and '생산지' (where something is made).

examples.en: In the movie, a shaman heals the villagers.

examples.ko: 그 주술사는 불 앞에서 이상한 주문을 외웠어요.
examples.en: The shaman chanted a strange spell in front of the fire.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들은 병이 나면 주술사를 찾아갔대요.
examples.en: I heard the villagers went to the shaman when they got sick.
The king asked the shaman about the future.
In this game, I created my character as a shaman.
He spoke in a low voice like a shaman.

explain: 주문이나 의식으로 신비한 힘을 쓴다고 믿어지는 사람이에요. 한국 전통에서 굿을 하는 사람은 '무당'이라고 하고, '주술사'는 여러 나라의 비슷한 사람을 넓게 가리켜요. 영화, 게임, 역사 이야기에서 자주 만나요.
explain_en: It refers to a person believed to use spells or rituals to wield mysterious power. In Korean tradition, a person who performs a 굿 ritual is called a '무당', while '주술사' broadly covers similar figures from many cultures. You will often meet it in movies, games and history stories.

examples.ko: 이 그림에는 주술적 의미가 담겨 있어요.
examples.en: This painting holds a magical, ritual meaning.

examples.ko: 옛사람들은 주술적 힘으로 병이 낫는다고 믿었어요.
examples.en: People in the past believed illness could be cured by magical power.

examples.ko: 그 노래는 주술적 분위기가 있어서 자꾸 들어요.
examples.en: That song has a hypnotic, incantation-like mood, so I keep listening.
Talismans were made for magical purposes.
The occult scene in the movie was so scary.

examples.ko: 이 의식은 종교적이면서 주술적 성격도 가져요.
examples.en: This ritual is religious and also has a magical character.

explain: 뒤에 명사가 와서 '주술적 의미', '주술적 힘'처럼 써요. 서술어로 쓸 때는 '주술적이다', '주술적인 분위기'처럼 '-이다'를 붙여요. '마법 같은'은 판타지 느낌이고, '주술적'은 믿음이나 의례와 관련된 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It goes before a noun, as in '주술적 의미' or '주술적 힘'. As a predicate or modifier, it takes '-이다', as in '주술적인 분위기'. '마법 같은' has a fantasy feel, while '주술적' feels more tied to belief and ritual.

examples.en: The main focus of this presentation is price.

examples.ko: 집을 고를 때 어디에 주안점을 두세요?
examples.en: What do you focus on most when choosing a home?

examples.ko: 이 수업의 주안점이 뭔지 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me what the main focus of this class is.
I bought the bag with convenience as my main priority.
I reorganized the materials to match the main focus.

examples.ko: 회의에서는 주안점 몇 가지만 짚고 넘어가요.
examples.en: In the meeting, we'll just go over a few key points.

explain: '주안점을 두다'처럼 자주 쓰고, 계획이나 발표에서 특히 중요하게 보는 부분을 말해요. '중점'과 비슷하지만 '주안점'은 글이나 회의에서 조금 더 격식 있게 들려요. 일상 대화에서는 '포인트'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is often used in '주안점을 두다' and refers to the part you treat as especially important in a plan or presentation. It is close to '중점' but sounds a bit more formal in writing and meetings. In everyday talk, people also say '포인트'.

examples.en: This album is full of gem-like songs.

examples.ko: 이 시집에 실린 시들은 모두 주옥같아요.
examples.en: Every poem in this collection is a gem.

examples.ko: 그 감독의 영화는 대사 하나하나가 주옥같았어요.
examples.en: Every line of dialogue in that director's film was a gem.

examples.ko: 주옥같이 아름다운 글이라서 몇 번씩 읽었어요.
examples.en: It was such a jewel of a piece of writing that I read it several times.
I was really happy to hear it praised as a gem.
The lyrics are exquisite and the melody is good too.

explain: 구슬이나 옥처럼 귀하고 아름답다는 칭찬이에요. 주로 글, 노래, 말씀, 명장면처럼 작품이나 말에 써요. 보통 '주옥같은 + 명사'로 많이 쓰고, 조금 격식 있고 글 같은 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is praise meaning something is as precious and beautiful as a jewel. It is mainly used for writing, songs, words of wisdom and famous scenes. It usually appears as '주옥같은 + noun' and sounds a bit formal and literary.

examples.en: The main ingredient of tofu is soybeans.

examples.ko: 이 과자의 주원료가 쌀가루라고 쓰여 있어요.
examples.en: It says the main ingredient of this snack is rice flour.
I heard they changed the main ingredient to a domestic one.

examples.ko: 김치의 주원료로 배추를 가장 많이 써요.
examples.en: Napa cabbage is the most common main ingredient of kimchi.

examples.ko: 주원료 외에 다른 재료도 조금 넣어요.
examples.en: Besides the main ingredient, I add a few other things too.
Snacks with rice as the main ingredient are easy to digest.

explain: 포장지의 성분표나 제품 설명에서 자주 보는 말이에요. '재료'는 요리까지 두루 쓰고 '원료'는 제품을 만드는 재료에 더 가까워요. 요리에서 가장 중요한 재료는 보통 '주재료'라고 해요.
explain_en: You often see this on packaging labels and product descriptions. '재료' is general and includes cooking, while '원료' leans toward materials used to make products. For the key ingredient in a recipe, people usually say '주재료'.

examples.ko: 주입식 교육은 학생이 스스로 생각할 기회가 적어요.
examples.en: Rote-style education gives students few chances to think for themselves.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 수업은 주입식이라서 좀 지루해요.
examples.en: Classes at my school are cram-style, so they're a bit boring.
Things I memorized by rote, I forget quickly.
Discussion-style classes are more fun than lecture-and-memorize ones.

examples.ko: 요즘은 주입식에서 벗어나려는 학교가 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: These days, more schools are trying to move away from rote teaching.

examples.ko: 주입식은 시험 준비에는 도움이 되지만 오래 기억하긴 어려워요.
examples.en: Cramming helps with exam prep, but it's hard to remember things long term.

explain: 거의 '주입식 교육'이나 '주입식 수업'처럼 가르치고 배우는 방식을 말할 때 써요. 반대로 쓰는 말은 '토론식', '체험식' 등이고, '암기식'과 비슷해요. 대체로 비판하는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is almost always used for teaching and learning methods, as in '주입식 교육' or '주입식 수업'. Its opposites include '토론식' and '체험식', and it is close to '암기식'. It usually carries a critical tone.

en: push someone to sit; have someone sit

examples.en: Mom made the child who was trying to stand up sit back down.
My friend grabs me as I try to leave and makes me sit back down.

examples.ko: 누가 날 주저앉히려고 해도 포기하지 않을 거예요.
examples.en: Even if someone tries to knock me down, I won't give up.
A big failure couldn't bring him down.

examples.ko: 코치는 흥분한 선수의 어깨를 눌러 의자에 주저앉혔어요.
examples.en: The coach pressed down on the agitated player's shoulders and forced him into the chair.

examples.ko: 걱정이 마음을 주저앉히기 전에 먼저 움직여요.
examples.en: I move first, before worry crushes my spirit.

explain: '주저앉다'(스스로 털썩 앉다)의 사동 표현이에요. 사람을 힘으로 눌러 앉히는 뜻과, 의욕이나 기세를 꺾어서 포기하게 만든다는 비유 뜻이 있어요. 그냥 '앉히다'는 부드럽게 앉게 하는 것이고 '주저앉히다'는 힘이 느껴져요.
explain_en: It is the causative of '주저앉다' (to plop down on one's own). It can mean forcing a person to sit, and figuratively crushing someone's drive so they give up. Plain '앉히다' is a gentle seating, while '주저앉히다' feels forceful.

examples.en: He hesitated and couldn't bring himself to speak.

examples.ko: 아이가 문 앞에서 주저주저 서 있었어요.
examples.en: The child stood hesitating at the door.
I dithered and hesitated, and finally missed the chance.

examples.ko: 손을 들까 말까 주저주저 눈치만 봤어요.
examples.en: I just hesitated, wondering whether to raise my hand or not.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 주저주저 대답하더니 고개를 숙였어요.
examples.en: He answered hesitantly and then lowered his head.
She walked over hesitantly and sat next to me.

explain: 선뜻 행동하지 못하고 머뭇거리는 모양이에요. '머뭇머뭇'과 뜻이 비슷하지만 '주저주저'는 할지 말지 망설이는 마음이 더 강해요. 반대 느낌으로는 '주저 없이'를 써요.
explain_en: It shows someone unable to act readily and wavering. It is close to '머뭇머뭇', but '주저주저' puts more weight on being torn about whether to do it. For the opposite feeling, use '주저 없이' (without hesitation).

examples.ko: 영화 볼 때 주전부리를 사 갈까요?
examples.en: Shall we buy some snacks to bring when we watch the movie?

examples.ko: 할머니 댁에 가면 주전부리가 항상 많아요.
examples.en: There are always lots of snacks at Grandma's house.
I eat fruit or nuts as snacks.

examples.ko: 밤에 주전부리 때문에 자꾸 살이 쪄요.
examples.en: I keep gaining weight because of late-night snacking.
Snacking is really hard to quit.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때는 주전부리도 꼭 챙겨요.
examples.en: When I travel, I always pack snacks too.

explain: 끼니 사이에 입이 심심해서 이것저것 먹는 과자, 과일 같은 간식을 말해요. '간식'보다 가볍고 친근한 느낌이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '군것질'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the snacks, such as crackers or fruit, that you nibble on between meals when your mouth feels bored. It sounds lighter and more casual than '간식'. '군것질' is also commonly used with the same meaning.

examples.en: It's my habit to snack while reading.
Even though I've had dinner, I keep wanting to snack.
Don't snack. Have your meal first.

examples.ko: 오후 내내 주전부리해서 배가 안 고파요.
examples.en: I snacked all afternoon, so I'm not hungry.
The kids snacked while watching the movie.
We chatted in the park while snacking.

explain: 식사가 아니라 끼니 사이에 이것저것 입에 넣는 것을 말해요. '간식을 먹다'보다 가벼운 느낌이고, '군것질하다'와 거의 같아요. '주전부리를 하다'처럼 띄어서 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It means munching on this and that between meals rather than eating a proper meal. It feels lighter than '간식을 먹다' and is nearly the same as '군것질하다'. It can also be written as '주전부리를 하다'.

examples.en: He walked off, mumbling something to himself.

examples.ko: 뭘 그렇게 주절거려요? 잘 안 들려요.
examples.en: What are you muttering on about? I can't hear you well.
My friend rambled on the phone for a long time.
The child began babbling before falling asleep.

examples.ko: 혼자 주절거리지 말고 크게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't mutter to yourself. Please say it out loud.
Grandpa keeps muttering away while watching TV.

explain: 낮은 목소리로 알아듣기 어렵게 말을 길게 늘어놓는 모습이에요. '중얼거리다'는 작게 혼잣말하는 느낌이 중심이고, '주절거리다'는 쓸데없는 말을 쭉 이어 가는 느낌이 더 있어요. 조금 가볍거나 못마땅한 말투예요.
explain_en: It describes going on at length in a low, hard-to-catch voice. '중얼거리다' centers on quiet self-talk, while '주절거리다' adds the feel of a stream of aimless words. The tone is a bit casual or disapproving.

examples.en: My friend rambled on, lamenting their situation.
He kept rattling off excuses.

examples.ko: 아이가 주절주절 하루 있었던 일을 이야기해요.
examples.en: The child chatters on about what happened during the day.
The teacher's talk dragged on and on, and it was boring.
I could hear a droning voice through the phone.
My senior suddenly started rambling on about old stories.

explain: 말을 쓸데없이 길게 이어 가는 모양이에요. '술술'은 막힘없이 잘 말하는 좋은 느낌이지만 '주절주절'은 길고 지루하다는 느낌이 있어요. '주절거리다'와 같은 계열의 말이에요.
explain_en: It shows words dragging on in a long, aimless stream. '술술' means speaking smoothly in a positive way, but '주절주절' feels long and tedious. It belongs to the same family as '주절거리다'.

examples.ko: 음식 앞에서 너무 주접스럽게 굴지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't act so greedy in front of food.

examples.ko: 동생이 먹는 모습이 좀 주접스러워 보여요.
examples.en: The way my younger sibling eats looks a bit gluttonous.

examples.ko: 그렇게 주접스러운 행동은 하지 않았으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope you won't behave in such an embarrassingly excessive way.
I'm embarrassed about how over-the-top I acted in front of the celebrity.
My friend teased me for being so over-the-top.
I looked so embarrassingly excessive that my face turned red.

explain: 먹을 것이나 좋아하는 것 앞에서 체면 없이 지나치게 구는 모습을 흉볼 때 써요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '주접스러워요', '주접스러운'으로 바뀌어요. '주접을 떨다'라는 표현도 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is used to tease or criticize someone who acts shamelessly over the top in front of food or something they love. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '주접스러워요' and '주접스러운'. It's also worth knowing the related expression '주접을 떨다'.

en: tactless; silly (acting without sense of time and place)

examples.ko: 제가 주책없이 너무 오래 이야기했나 봐요.
examples.en: I think I talked on way too long without any sense of timing.
Please don't mock me for being silly at my age.
I said something tactless, and the mood got awkward.

examples.ko: 저는 주책없어서 비밀을 잘 못 지켜요.
examples.en: I'm so thoughtless that I can't keep secrets well.
I burst out laughing at the wrong moment and got in trouble.
I'm sorry, I'm a tactless and clueless person.

explain: 때와 장소를 가리지 않고 말하거나 행동해서 어이없고 실없어 보일 때 써요. 나이 든 사람이 감정이 북받치거나 푼수 같은 행동을 할 때 스스로 '내가 주책이지'라고 말하기도 해요. 일상에서는 '주책이야'처럼 짧게 말하는 경우도 많아요.
explain_en: It describes talking or acting without regard for time and place, so you seem silly or tactless. People, especially older ones, sometimes say '내가 주책이지' about themselves when overcome by emotion or acting goofy. In daily speech, it is often shortened to '주책이야'.

examples.en: At a shareholders' meeting, agenda items are usually passed by majority vote.

examples.ko: 주총의 의결 사항은 홈페이지에서 확인할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can check the resolutions of the shareholders' meeting on the website.

examples.ko: 이번 주총은 다음 달 말에 열려요.
examples.en: This shareholders' meeting will be held at the end of next month.

examples.ko: 주총에 참석하지 못하면 위임장을 보낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you can't attend the shareholders' meeting, you can send a proxy form.

examples.ko: 많은 회사가 비슷한 시기에 주총을 열어요.
examples.en: Many companies hold their shareholders' meetings around the same time.
The results of the shareholders' meeting were on the news.

explain: '주주총회'의 줄임말이에요. 뉴스나 경제 기사에서 많이 나오고, 회사의 주식을 가진 사람들이 모여 중요한 일을 결정하는 자리예요. 말할 때나 기사 제목에서는 줄여서 '주총'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the short form of '주주총회'. It appears often in news and economic articles, and refers to the meeting where people who own shares of a company gather to decide important matters. In speech and headlines, it is shortened to '주총'.

examples.en: He hesitated in front of the door and then came in.

examples.ko: 갑자기 개가 나타나서 저도 모르게 주춤거렸어요.
examples.en: A dog suddenly appeared, and I flinched without meaning to.
Don't hang back. Come in quickly.
The child hangs back in front of strangers.
The way he answered, faltering, looked awkward.
The person ahead hesitated, and the line got blocked.

explain: 놀라거나 망설여서 동작을 잠깐 멈추거나 뒤로 물러나는 모습이에요. '주저하다'는 마음속 망설임에 가깝고, '주춤거리다'는 몸의 움직임이 눈에 보여요. '주춤하다'라고도 써요.
explain_en: It shows someone briefly stopping or drawing back out of surprise or uncertainty. '주저하다' is closer to inner hesitation, while '주춤거리다' is visible in the body's movement. You can also say '주춤하다'.

examples.en: In a hanok, a foundation stone is placed under each pillar.

examples.ko: 튼튼한 주춧돌 위에 집을 지어야 안전해요.
examples.en: A house is safe only when built on a solid foundation stone.

examples.ko: 이 경험이 제 성공의 주춧돌이 되었어요.
examples.en: This experience became the foundation of my success.
My parents are the cornerstone of our family.

examples.ko: 오래된 주춧돌만 남아 있는 절터에 갔어요.
examples.en: I visited a temple site where only the old foundation stones remain.
I think studying the basics is the foundation of skill.

explain: 기둥 밑에 받쳐 놓는 돌인데, 비유로 '무엇의 바탕이 되는 것'이라는 뜻으로도 많이 써요. 한자어 '초석'과 뜻이 같고 글에서 조금 더 딱딱하게 들려요. 사람이나 경험이 바탕이 될 때 '~의 주춧돌이 되다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 선생님께서 제 인생의 주춧돌을 놓아 주셨어요.
phrases.en: My teacher laid the foundation of my life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 돌이 아니라 앞으로 일이 잘되도록 기초를 마련한다는 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is figurative rather than literal, meaning to prepare the groundwork so that later things go well.

explain_en: It is the stone set beneath a pillar, and it is also widely used figuratively for the base of something. The Sino-Korean '초석' means the same and sounds a bit stiffer in writing. You say '~의 주춧돌이 되다' when a person or experience becomes the basis of something.

en: bead; counter; bead on the abacus

examples.en: Grandpa calculates by flicking the abacus beads quickly.

examples.ko: 주판알이 하나 빠져서 계산이 안 돼요.
examples.en: One abacus bead is missing, so I can't calculate.
Children learn numbers with colored abacus beads.
The old abacus beads are smooth and shiny from being handled.
One abacus bead fell on the floor.
Every abacus bead is strung on a rod.

explain: 주판 전체는 '주판'이고, 그 위에서 움직이는 구슬 하나하나가 '주판알'이에요. '주판알을 튕기다'는 이익과 손해를 따진다는 비유로도 써요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 이익만 따지며 주판알을 튕기고 있어요.
phrases.en: He is only weighing up profit, crunching the numbers in his head.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이익과 손해를 꼼꼼히 따져 계산한다는 뜻이고, 속셈이 보여서 조금 못마땅한 느낌이 있을 때가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means carefully calculating gain and loss, often with a disapproving hint of calculated self-interest.

explain_en: The whole device is '주판', and each moving bead on it is a '주판알'. '주판알을 튕기다' is also used figuratively for weighing up gain and loss.

examples.en: The car ahead suddenly slowed down in the driving lane.
After overtaking, return to the driving lane.
I'm driving slowly along the driving lane.
There are many trucks in the driving lane of the highway.
The driving lane was backed up, so I was late for work.
It's dangerous to confuse the driving lane with the shoulder.

explain: 도로에서 차가 일반적으로 달리는 차선을 말하고, 운전 교육이나 도로 설명에서 많이 나와요. 앞차를 지나갈 때 쓰는 차선은 '추월선'이라고 해서 서로 구분해요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '차선'이나 '1차로, 2차로'처럼 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It refers to the lane where vehicles normally travel, and appears mostly in driving lessons and road explanations. The lane used for passing the car ahead is called '추월선', so the two are distinguished. In everyday talk, people usually just say '차선' or '1차로, 2차로'.
